title: All-purpose citrus cleaning spray
subtitle: A simple dilute-and-go surface cleaner
excerpt: A light cleaning spray of white vinegar, water, and citrus essential oils. Cuts grease on worktops, tiles, and sealed surfaces without leaving residue. Makes 400 ml; keeps a year.
sourceNotes: Acetic acid cleaning action: Cosgrove, D. et al., 'Antimicrobial activity of household cleaners', International Journal of Food Microbiology (open-access review, 2002). Essential-oil phototoxicity notes: IFRA guidelines for cold-pressed citrus oils (2020), published at ifrafragrance.org. White vinegar and natural stone caution: Marble Institute of America care guidelines (freely available at marble-institute.com).

recipe.batchNotes: Doubles to 800 ml for two bottles. Keep the proportions the same.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Mix fresh when needed; a batch in a labelled bottle keeps easily in the cupboard.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: Keeps one year in a sealed spray bottle in a cupboard. Discard if the spray turns cloudy or develops an off smell.

glossaryTerms.definition: The active acid in vinegar, typically at 5% in household white vinegar. It dissolves mineral deposits, cuts light grease, and reduces surface bacteria.

content.text: This is a dilute vinegar-and-citrus spray for worktops, tiles, sealed wood surfaces, and bathroom fittings. The

in the vinegar dissolves mineral scale and cuts light kitchen grease; the citrus essential oils leave the surface smelling clean. Not for natural stone (marble, limestone, granite) or unfinished wood.

items.prepNote: tap water works but distilled avoids water-marks
cold-pressed; phototoxic; rinse-off product is safe at this dilution
1 tsp unscented Castile; boosts surface wetting slightly; omit on glass to avoid streaks

content.text: Pour the white vinegar into the spray bottle.
Drop in the lemon and sweet orange essential oils.
If using, add the Castile soap last.
Fit the spray cap and shake gently to combine. Shake before each use.

Works on sealed kitchen worktops, ceramic and porcelain tiles, stainless steel, sealed wood, and bathroom fittings. Do not use on natural stone surfaces (marble, limestone, granite, travertine) as the acid etches them. Do not use on unfinished or oiled wood. Phototoxic citrus oils in a rinse-off product at this dilution are safe on surfaces; they are not a leave-on skin product.

Store in a labelled, sealed spray bottle in a cupboard. Keeps one year. Discard if the liquid turns cloudy or develops an off smell. The citrus essential oils will fade after six months; the cleaning action of the vinegar remains.
